component.name: BackAtIt
component.summary: Get up, walk it off, and actually get back at it

description.p: BackAtIt started with back pain. Sitting through long stretches of work without moving does that, and every break reminder I tried was far too easy to wave away — a small notification in the corner, dismissed without even reading it, and another hour gone.

So this one is harder to ignore. When a break is due it takes over the whole screen and sounds an alarm, and it ignores the keyboard completely, so carrying on typing cannot dismiss it by accident. You get up because it is genuinely easier to get up than to argue with it.

The other half is the part most timers forget: coming back. Once your break is over a second alert calls you back to the desk and keeps nagging — a burst of alarm, then a longer and longer silence — until you answer it. No more twenty-minute five-minute breaks.
Everything about it bends to how you actually work:

ul.li: Break interval, break length and snooze, all down to half a minute
Both alerts say whatever you want them to say
Runs on a daily schedule, with any combination of days off — not just weekends
Stays quiet when you are already away instead of alarming an empty room
Your own choice of sound for each alert
A tally of the breaks you actually took, over the last week or month

description.p: Written for anyone whose back, eyes, wrists or posture are paying for their screen time — and for anyone whose pomodoro timer has quietly become part of the furniture.

description.p: Removing a home-directory install no longer leaves GTK warning about a missing icon, and the built-in guide describes away detection on every supported desktop.
The Snooze and Turn off reminders buttons and the hold-to-unlock bar now work during a locked break; before, the lock held them too.
New installs lock the screen for the whole break and start at login by default. Existing setups keep their own choices.
Works on every mainstream Linux desktop — GNOME, KDE Plasma, XFCE, Cinnamon, MATE and Budgie — and now also comes as a package for Fedora and openSUSE.

On KDE Plasma the locked break now really holds the keyboard and mouse, and skipping a break when you are already away works on every desktop rather than only on GNOME. Notifications clear themselves instead of piling up in your notification list.
Brings the bundled user guide up to date: it still described the app under its old name and pointed at directories that have not been used since before 1.0, and it predated the screen lock entirely.

The hold-to-unlock duration, the length of the alarm on a locked break and the input lock's safety margin can now be set in the config file, alongside the other advanced settings. Previously they could only be changed by editing the program.
Puts Snooze back on a locked break, where 1.3 had dropped it. The break has already started by then, so snoozing abandons it and puts the next one off by your snooze length.

The alerts now size themselves to the screen they land on, so the wording stays in proportion on a laptop panel instead of filling it. Each alert's buttons sit in one row at a matching size, and Turn off reminders is easier to find without becoming something you drift into by accident.

Fixes an About card that rendered completely blank when the name, version or licence in about.conf contained an ampersand or an angle bracket. Sound previews in the settings window now use whichever player is installed rather than assuming PipeWire, and a locked break that is killed from a console is no longer recorded as one you saw through.

Redraws both full-screen alerts. The time left is now the largest thing on screen with a bar filling as the break runs, and the two alerts are colour-coded — amber to get up, green to come back — so you can tell them apart from across the room without reading them.
The three-second delay before buttons become clickable now applies only where a stray click would cost you something. Coming back to work, and the hold-to-unlock bar, respond immediately.

A locked break no longer waits to be acknowledged. The screen is locked the moment the alarm sounds, so there is nothing to press: the break starts counting down there and then, and the alarm is a short burst rather than a minute and a half of it.

Unlocking early with the hold button now only ends that break. The next one arrives as it always would have, and only Turn off reminders stops them for the day. Breaks cut short this way are counted separately, so the tally still says how many you saw through.

Fixes an upgrade that appeared to work but did not. The background app is a long-running process that reads its code once at startup, and the package failed to stop it, so an upgraded machine carried on running the previous version until the next login. Anyone who upgraded to 1.2 and found the new screen lock did nothing was hitting this.

Adds an option to lock the screen for the whole break, not just for the alert. The alert stays up for the entire break, takes over the mouse and keyboard and blanks your other monitors, so there is no moment where you could quietly sit back down. Hold the unlock button for five seconds to get out early.
Fixes a stale-state bug that could leave the window showing an out-of-date countdown and refusing to start, and stops the Stop button from cancelling a daily schedule that was not running.
First release.
